method.isa: Correlate rocprofv3 kernel_object-load_base to the exact hipBLASLt descriptor, zstd-decompress its CCOB payload, unbundle gfx950 HSACO, and disassemble from the selected global symbol to the next global function.
method.raw_trace_policy: Raw profiler databases and CSVs remain local and uncommitted.

static_isa_audit.caveat: hipBLASLt universal symbols contain guarded edge, user-argument, activation, and alternative epilogue paths. Static counts are diagnostic upper bounds, not dynamic instruction counts.

ssa_algebra_conclusion: The online QVQ graph contains no SU/SV multiply, Hadamard butterfly, packed decode, bank selection, xor-shift, hash, level lookup, or finite reduction for enabled shapes; those operations are folded into the mutation-aware cache.
For bias-free profitable regimes, FP32 accumulation now narrows in the selected hipBLASLt epilogue, eliminating the standalone cast allocation, read, write, and launch.

M1 still has a library-selected GSU8 reduction after its main GEMM. Dispatch/layout/split sweeps found no generally faster library configuration; a one-pass dense GEMV is the remaining plausible tiny-M experiment.
KV M4096 and linear-Z M512 deliberately retain the standalone cast because direct-FP16-output hipBLASLt algorithms regress end-to-end latency there.
All recurring kernels have zero scratch; remaining integer/address algebra belongs to hipBLASLt universal kernels rather than source-level QVQ redundancy.

decision.next_candidate: A one-pass gfx950 dense GEMV specialized for M1 may remove the library GSU8 reduction, but it is lower priority because the requested full-matrix speedup is already exceeded and must preserve the current accuracy/VRAM contract.
